I am fifty-three years old and have been farming these lands in Quzhou since I was a young man. I only finished primary school, so I never learned much from books, but I learned plenty from my father and from watching what works in the fields around our village. Every year I start with what I did last year and make small adjustments based on what my neighbors tried and how the weather looks.

This year I will stick to the same cropping system that most families here use. My winter wheat is already in the ground from last October on eight mu of my best flat land. I will manage it through to harvest in early June, then immediately plant summer maize on that same land — there is barely a week between harvest and planting, so there is no time for deep tillage. I will plant the maize directly into the wheat stubble using no-tillage, just like everyone else does now. On another four mu of land I will grow cotton. It means a lot of time spraying, but cotton prices have been steady and my wife and I can manage the picking with some help from relatives.

For the wheat, I will use an improved variety — I have been using Jimai 22 and similar types for years and they give me about 500 jin per mu if the weather cooperates. Before planting last autumn I rotary-tilled the field and put down about 100 jin of compound fertilizer per mu. Now in spring I will topdress with urea at jointing and again at heading, about 50 jin of urea per mu in total. I would rather apply a little too much than risk a thin crop. I will irrigate three or four times depending on rainfall — the well water costs money but dry wheat is a disaster. I will spray for weeds and insects three or four times; last year aphids were bad so I will watch carefully.

For the summer maize, I will use Denghai 605, a hybrid seed that my neighbor used last year and got over 600 jin per mu. I will put down a little compound fertilizer at planting and maybe one bag of urea when the plants are knee-high — the wheat field already has some fertility left from before. I will irrigate twice, once when it is very hot in July and again when the ears are filling. Two or three sprays for weeds and borers should be enough.

For cotton, I will rotary-till the plot in April and plant an improved variety. Cotton needs a lot of care — I will spray almost every week for insects and weeds, maybe fourteen or fifteen times through the season. I will irrigate twice and put down some fertilizer at planting and once more when it flowers. I expect about 250 to 300 jin per mu of seed cotton.

I never calculate things precisely like the extension people tell us to. I look at what my neighbors do, I think about how much cash I have for inputs, and I make sure I do not cut corners on fertilizer because a bad harvest means borrowing money. That is how I have kept my family fed for thirty years and that is what I will do this year.
